questions.question: Explain how fractional distillation works?
questions.modelAnswer: Crude oil is heated until most of it turns to gas. The gases enter the base of the fractionating column. The fractionating column has a temperature gradient. It is hot at the bottom and cool at the top. The longer hydrocarbons have high boiling points so they condense at the bottom of the column (e.g. bitumen, heavy fuel oil and diesel oil). Shorter hydrocarbons have low boiling points so they condense at the top of the column (e.g. kerosene, petrol and liquified petroleum gas).
markingPoints: Crude oil is heated until most of it turns to gas. The gases enter the base of the fractionating column. The fractionating column has a temperature gradient. It is hot at the bottom and cool at the top. The longer hydrocarbons have high boiling points so they condense at the bottom of the column (e.g. bitumen, heavy fuel oil and diesel oil). Shorter hydrocarbons have low boiling points so they condense at the top of the column (e.g. kerosene, petrol and liquified petroleum gas).

questions.question: Describe the the two methods of cracking hydrocarbons?
